test_evidence.details: Untouched pre-change Go baseline passed in the official Go 1.23 container. The host has no Go executable, so the container is the reproducible test runtime.
Untouched pre-change React baseline passed: 1 suite and 1 test. It emitted the existing TitleComponent componentWillMount warning.

Final uncached source characterization passed. It covers real JWT/JWKS middleware for missing, malformed, valid, matching, mismatched, expired, wrong-audience, and missing-subject credentials; feelings and weekly success/empty/invalid/identity/query/upsert behavior through real Gin handlers with Mongo wire mocks; and legacy CORS plus unmatched ping behavior.

Final React suite passed: 2 suites and 3 tests. New tests verify current Auth0 audience, bearer and x-user-id headers, routes, query parameters, and feelings/weekly request payloads. The pre-existing TitleComponent lifecycle warning remains characterized and unchanged.
The base-URL-driven source/target smoke runner is syntactically valid. It requires explicit CONTRACT_BASE_URL and optional isolated test credentials at execution time and embeds no credentials.
Runtime-neutral contract fixtures are valid JSON and contain only synthetic identities and content.
The source plan remained structurally valid, ready, and approved while Stage 1 was implemented.

stages.notes: Stage 1 changed tests, test-only module metadata, fixtures, and migration documentation only; server/main.go, server/handlers.go, and runtime React behavior were not modified. Characterized source quirks include null empty feelings, unsorted feeling reads, permissive/inconsistent validation errors, empty-200 CORS rejection, and an unmatched client ping. The replacement must follow the approved normalized design rather than copy those quirks. Repository search plus Vinicius Delascio's Define-stage confirmation provides the current evidence that the OpenClaw/chat/agent routes have no caller; no production logs, secrets, private data, or external systems were accessed.
